components.gap: Routed treatment (early-medieval-latin-logic.tex) reconstructs most of Marenbon ch.1 but not every actual definition/argument case/example/qualification. Missing on the route: the Introduction's two stated reasons for studying the period and its social-history-of-logic programme (ms pp.1-2); Apuleius's dating/authorship discussion and Kenny's proposal that Marius Victorinus wrote the Ten Categories (p.5); Martianus Capella's dating (p.6); the subsection 'Boethian Logic and its Survival' (two ancient Latin traditions, the twelfth-century Golden Age of Boethian logic and its 13th-14th-century decline, pp.20-21); the Boethian question-form 'Either A is B or A is not B' and the Book IV rhetorical topics (p.19); the source's numbered argument (12)-(14) with added premiss (13a) and its specific analytic maximal-proposition examples (cause; modus ponens) (pp.19-20); Alcuin's De vera philosophia preface, the verbatim Cassiodorus/Isidore copying and the source-less Chapter XII on arguments (p.23); the Epilogue 5.4 content (Anselm's flatum vocis charge against Roscelin, divine-mind Platonic universals together with immanent realism, the 1100 periodisation thesis and Marenbon's self-correction about William of Champeaux's commentaries, pp.56-57).
